reden: Yes. The audit report explicitly identifies reentrancy in FeeAMM.sol::burn() caused by performing external token transfers before updating liquidity/reserve accounting (CEI violation). It explains that a token with transfer/receive hooks (ERC777-style or malicious) or a recipient callback can re-enter burn() before state is reduced, enabling multiple payouts from the same liquidity and mentions underflow risks in pre-0.8 compilers. This matches the vulnerability description’s mechanism, code path, and impact, and would be fixed by the same remediation (apply CEI or add a reentrancy guard).
